items.title: Andy Taylor, Former Duran Duran Guitarist, Dead at 65
items.summary:
Andy Taylor , guitarist and former member of Duran Duran , has died after a yearslong battle with prostate cancer. He was 65 years old.

Related 

Former Duran Duran Member Andy Taylor Misses Rock Hall of Fame Induction Because of Stage 4 Cancer 

Duran Duran’s Andy Taylor Says Cancer Drug Has Extended His Life Five More Years 

Gone But Not Forgotten: Musicians We Lost in 2026 

The musician’s former bandmates shared the news Wednesday (Nov. 25) on their website and on Instagram , announcing that Taylor had passed away two days prior. “Andy was there at the very beginning of our story,” the group wrote. “From the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East with a guitar and an unshakeable belief in what we could become, he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music.”

Duran Duran continued, “His playing drove the songs that took us around the world, and with a dry wit that was matched only by his wonderfully unsentimental, no-nonsense outlook on life he kept us grounded and gave the band its edge through the extraordinary years that followed.”

Still in its early years, the band added Taylor to the lineup in 1980. He would leave in 1986 before rejoining in 2001, playing guitar on Duran Duran’s 2004 album Astronaut (which reached No. 17 on the Billboard 200 ) before leaving again in 2006. In 2023, he’d contribute guitar to Halloween-themed LP Danse Macabre .

During his time in the group, Duran Duran scored 13 hits on the Billboard Hot 100 , including two No. 1s: “The Reflex” in 1984 and “A View to a Kill” in 1985. The group’s blockbuster Rio album (which…

When the team at the LOS40 group of radio stations began defining the lineup for the LOS40 Music Awards Santander 2026, someone asked a seemingly simple question: “Which Spanish artist is going to perform?” What surprised Vicent Argudo, director of music at the parent company Prisa Media, most wasn’t the question itself but the fact that, until that moment, no one had considered it. The list of performers included Puerto Rican Eladio Carrión , Argentine Emilia and Colombian Carlos Vives .

items.title: Publishing Briefs: Believe & GL Music Form JV, Gram Parsons to Be Administered by Peermusic
items.summary:
Believe Music Publishing and GL Music Entertainment have formed a joint venture, which sees Believe Music Publishing administering GL Music Entertainment’s catalog.

GL Music Entertainment was founded by Kim Nowak-Zorde , Daniel Fält and Lasse Lindorff , who also all work as songwriters and producers. Lindorff serves as the company’s CEO, Nowak-Zorde as head of entertainment and Christan Fløe Svenningsen is publishing director. Artists on the company’s roster has written and produced songs for Kylie Minogue, BTS, Julie Bergan and more. GL Music largely works with K-pop, J-pop and C-pop.

“The partnership with Believe Music Publishing gives us the global infrastructure, an even stronger international network and resources to take that ambition to another level, while allowing GL Music Entertainment to remain independent, entrepreneurial and creatively focused.”

Pete McCamley , who serves as vp of publishing at Believe, said, “Having worked with GL Music Entertainment from a distance for many years, I am delighted to work much closer with Lasse & Christian through our new venture. They have built a great creative business that operates on songwriter-first principles, with an incredibly strong track record across territories and genres. I’m excited to see the results of this new collaboration and be part of this next chapter.”

Chris Meehan , CEO of publishing at Believe, added, “Lasse, Kim and Christian always put songwriters first, and you can feel that in everything GL Music Entertainment does. Their writers have made their mark everywhere from the Nordics to K-pop, and…
items.t: Publishing Briefs: Believe & GL Music Form JV, Gram Parsons to Be Administered by Peermusic

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album review – even GTA sceptics will warm to this zeitgeisty, star-packed soundtrack
items.summary:
(Atlantic)
Justice bring some 80s nostalgia but this compilation of new material from music’s A-list – from Dua Lipa to Travis Scott and a host of Latin talent – stays at the cutting edge

It can be hard to ascertain why Grand Theft Auto VI is such a phenomenon from merely watching along with it. Equally devoted to the thrill of a violent crime story and a more mundane lifestyle fantasy, the appeal does not always translate to bystanders. Its soundtrack, however, is another story: a compilation of brand new material from some of the biggest pop, rap, rock and country artists on the planet – some of them combined in imaginative pileups of guest features – that can be enjoyed totally separately from the gameplay, if you so wish.

Starting from Zero, the opener by Justice – also composers of the game’s original score, released on 11 December – features the unmistakable voice of the Doobie Brothers’ Michael McDonald belting out an 80s-style pop ballad complete with a saxophone outro. This style is synonymous with Grand Theft Auto VI’s setting, a fictionalised version of Florida last seen in 2002’s Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, which was beloved for its inclusion of 80s hits.

Continue reading...
items.t: Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album review – even GTA sceptics will warm to this zeitgeisty, star-packed soundtrack

items.title: Jungle announce run of huge summer 2027 UK shows
items.summary:
Jungle have announced a run of massive UK shows for next summer, including a headline slot at Latitude .

READ MORE: Jungle interview: “I spent three years trying to make another ‘Busy Earnin’” 

The dates come in support of the BRIT-award winning trio dropping their uplifting fifth album ‘ Sunshine ’ earlier this year – their first since 2023’s ‘ Volcano ’.

Dates kick off at Bristol’s Queen Square on June 19 and will be one of the first concerts held at the outdoor space since Massive Attack performed a landmark set there in 2003. For over two decades there were no shows held there, until IDLES hosted a huge Block Party there last summer.

Jungle’s performance will follow the same sustainable initiative that IDLES had in place, becoming one of the first large-scale events of their kind in the UK to be powered entirely by batteries and the national grid, without a generator in sight.

View this post on Instagram 

The group have also been confirmed as a headliner for Latitude 2027, which returns to Henham Park in Southwold between July 22 and 25. It will be their first slot there since playing on the Second Stage back in 2014, and the other two headliners will be confirmed at a later date.

“We’re super excited to be heading back to Latitude in 2027,” the trio shared. “It’s one of the first festivals we ever played in the UK and to be asked to headline the Obelisk Arena next summer is an honour and we can’t wait.”

On July 25, they’ll perform at Brighton’s On The Beach festival, joining Two Door Cinema Club , Tom Jones , Pete Tong and more as headliners, and on July 31…
items.t: Jungle announce run of huge summer 2027 UK shows

items.title: Andy Burnham says UK government have “negotiated language that may make it easier in future for British bands, performers and artists to tour in Europe”
items.summary:
Andy Burnham has addressed the issues facing artists across the UK, and said that the government has “negotiated language that may make it easier in future for British bands, performers and artists to tour in Europe”.

READ MORE: UK touring bands are suffering due to “Brexit fuck-ups and a lack of government control” 

The Prime Minister made the comments in parliament, highlighting the widespread issues facing musicians looking to tour, including rising costs and Brexit – the latter of which putting an end to visa-free travel for UK artists and crew wishing to work and creating an existential threat to the talent pipeline .

Speaking about “touring musicians and artists”, Burnham said that he was “particularly pleased” that his parliament had “negotiated language that may make it easier in the future for British bands, performers and artists to tour in Europe”.

Addressing the threats facing the sector, he said that music is “arguably our finest export”, but also “an area we are in danger of taking too much for granted”.

“British music is known and loved around the world. Brexit made it harder to tour, but we now have a chance to explore mutually beneficial solutions,” he added. “We still have work to do, but let me say directly to all our musicians, I fully intend to take this opportunity.”

Burnham’s comments addressing the touring situation for artists following Brexit comes as he attended a major summit in Brussels on Friday (November 20), where the EU and UK announced a new UK–EU “reset” deal that affected food and drink, emissions trading and a youth mobility…
items.t: Andy Burnham says UK government have “negotiated language that may make it easier in future for British bands, performers and artists to tour in Europe”

items.title: Bonehead to raffle iconic signed Oasis Live ’25 cut-out of himself for charity
items.summary:
Paul “Bonehead” Arthurs is raffling off the life-sized cut-out of himself that Oasis brought out on the Live ‘25 tour , and donating the money to charity.

READ MORE: Oasis live in Cardiff: a supersonic reunion for a new generation 

The cut-out was made after the original and founding guitarist for Oasis was unable to make several shows on the iconic Live ‘25 reunion tour last year as he was undergoing treatment for prostate cancer.

He was given the all-clear from tonsil cancer back in 2022 , but shared early last year that he had been diagnosed with prostate cancer. He then shared an update in October 2025, saying that he would be taking a “planned break” from the shows and sitting out the band’s dates in Asia and Australia so that he could get “the next phase of care”. He later rejoined them for shows in South America towards the end of the year.

In his absence, Noel Gallagher arranged for a life-sized cardboard version of Bonehead to be made to join the group on tour. It was first seen on stage at a show in Goyang Stadium in Seoul , South Korea on October 21, and became a running joke, consistently appearing on stage with the group on various nights and dressed up in different themed outfits.

Now, Bonehead has signed the cut-out and teamed up with The Christie Charity to auction it off for charity. All proceeds will support cancer care and research at The Christie NHS Foundation Trust in Manchester – the hospital that treated him with both his diagnoses.

Bonehead cut-out being auctioned for Christie Foundation. CREDIT: Press

items.title: ‘Red Dead Redemption’ Hollywood adaptation on the table, reports claim
items.summary:
Rockstar Games is “more open” to teaming up with someone to make a Red Dead Redemption adaptation, claims a new report.

In 2024, Rockstar co-founder Dan Houser claimed the reason why no Grand Theft Auto or Red Dead Redemption adaptation had been made was because the studio wouldn’t have full creative control. “The risk never made sense. In those days, the perception was that games made poor-quality movies,” he told The Ankler . “It’s a different time now,” he added, with celebrated adaptations of The Last Of Us and Fallout .

According to a new report from The Ankler , Rockstar is now “more open” to bringing Red Dead Redemption to film or television, but it’ll be an expensive project. “At one point, they were throwing around a purchase price of more than $100 million minimum for licensing rights,” an agent who works with writers in the video game space told the outlet.

And if any potential studios are looking for an actor to take on the role of Red Dead Redemption protagonist Arthur Morgan, Jeffrey Dean Morgan has said he’d do it in a “heartbeat” .

The same report claims that Rockstar is still not interested in an adaptation of Grand Theft Auto “despite years of incoming calls from entertainment companies eager to adapt the blockbuster 30-year franchise.”

items.title: Matthew Perry’s grave headstone ‘Friends’ reference removed
items.summary:
The plaque on Matthew Perry ’s headstone has been updated to remove a reference to Friends .

Matthew Perry was found unresponsive in a hot tub in his Los Angeles home on October 28, 2023. He was later pronounced dead, with his death being attributed to the acute effects of ketamine , and drowning and coronary artery disease listed as other factors.

Earlier this year, Perry’s live-in assistant Kenneth Iwamasa was sentenced to three years and five months in jail after being found guilty of injecting the Friends star with ketamine after working with two doctors to secure $50,000 (£38,000) of the drug in the weeks leading up to his death.

Jasveen Sangha, the drug dealer also known as the ‘Ketamine Queen’, was sentenced to 15 years in prison for supplying the drugs that Perry took before his death while rehab counsellor Erik Fleming, Dr. Salvador Plasencia and Dr. Mark Chavez were also found guilty of supplying Perry with ketamine .

As reported by Entertainment Weekly , a new grave marker was placed on Perry’s grave in January that read: “Matthew Langford Perry. August 19, 1969 – October 28, 2023. Much Loved – Friend –”.

Recently though, that plaque has been replaced. The new headstone still features Perry’s full name but now reads “Rest now. We love you with our whole hearts”.

'Friends' star Matthew Perry's grave marker no longer references his 'Friends' role.

The new plaque at Forest Lawn Hollywood Hills replaces the "Much Loved, Friend" marker, which now reads "Rest Now" followed by "We Love You With Our Whole Hearts."

items.t: Matthew Perry’s grave headstone ‘Friends’ reference removed

items.title: New Order play first full gig without Stephen Morris and Gillian Gilbert in São Paulo: “We just want them to know how much we’re missing them”
items.summary:
New Order played their first full gig without Stephen Morris and Gillian Gilbert, and told fans about “how much we’re missing them”. Check out photos, footage and the setlist from the night below.

READ MORE: “It felt like we were changing the world”: inside New Order’s seminal ‘Power, Corruption & Lies’ 

The gig took place on Monday (November 23) as the first date of the band’s 2026 tour of South America, and the first of their two 8,000 capacity shows in Sao Paulo, Brazil.

Kicking off slightly later than usual due to severe weather, the gig was the first full gig since Gillian Gilbert announced that she would not be joining the group on the road due to health reasons. It was also the first full New Order show without drummer Stephen Morris, who has stepped back from international touring.

Morris was the drummer in Joy Division alongside Bernard Sumner , Peter Hook and Ian Curtis , and the remaining members formed New Order with Gilbert after Curtis’ death in 1980. Morris and Gilbert have also released music together outside New Order as The Other Two. Their debut album, ‘The Other Two & You’, arrived in 1993, followed by ‘Super Highways’ in 1999.

In June, New Order confirmed that both Morris and Gilbert would not be touring with them in the “foreseeable future” due to “personal” reasons, and in September, Gilbert told fans that she is living with cancer .

New Order in Sao Paulo, November 2026. CREDIT: @lali_moss

items.title: Patrick Stewart’s ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ wrap speech indicated it was “his last day on a film set”
items.summary:
The team behind Avengers: Doomsday have spoken about working with Patrick Stewart on what would become his last on-screen appearance.

Stewart died last month , aged 80. His family confirmed his passing in an Instagram post that explained the veteran actor had undergone “a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia”.

Before his death, Stewart reprised his role as Charles Xavier / Professor X in Avengers: Doomsday , a character he first played in 2000’s X-Men movie. When the movie launches next month, it will feature a tribute to Stewart. “We’re long done filming that movie, and he did an amazing job for us,” Marvel Studios boss Kevin Feige told Entertainment Weekly . “We’re looking now at how we can put something together that honours and respects our friend.”

“He stood up and he gave a speech to the crew [on the last day of principal photography]. We didn’t know necessarily it would be his last day on a set, but he was sort of indicating to us that he thought it was,” he added.

items.title: The Beatles’ new London 3 Savile Row plans approved by council – with “truly immersive experience” planned for rooftop
items.summary:
New plans for The Beatles ’ London 3 Savile Row have been approved by the council, and include a “truly immersive experience” taking place on the rooftop.

READ MORE: Paul McCartney interviewed: “Writing a song is still a magic feeling for me, and hopefully always will be” 

The site was the Apple Corps headquarters in London, and the place where ‘ Let It Be ‘ was recorded. It also was the spot where they played their iconic final public performance in 1969 on the rooftop.

Earlier this year, the company announced it was converting the building into a seven-floor “cultural experience and exhibition” celebrating The Beatles, with a basement café-bar on the site of the studio where they recorded their last album.

It is set to open its doors next year and include seven floors of never-before-seen material from Apple Corps’ extensive archives, rotating exhibitions, a fan store, and a recreation of the original studio where ‘Let it Be’ was recorded. An expected 900 visitors are expected to visit each weekday, and around 1,140 on the weekends – although it was recently confirmed that no live music can be played on the terrace and any amplified music or speech will have to be limited.

Now, it has been confirmed that the plans for 3 Savile Row have been given the seal of approval from the government, and include a “truly immersive experience” that will take place on the rooftop.

The Westminster City Council’s Planning Committee approved the plans last night (Tuesday November 24), confirming that fans will be able to visit the exhibitions, the basement recording studio, and the…
items.t: The Beatles’ new London 3 Savile Row plans approved by council – with “truly immersive experience” planned for rooftop

items.title: Post your questions for Carl Cox
items.summary:
Ahead of him rounding out the year at a huge London show, the DJ legend will join us to answer your questions

Beatifically smiling as he sends another packed dancefloor into raptures, Carl Cox is one of the most enduring and reliably euphoria-inducing figures in UK club culture history. As he prepares to close out the current season at Drumsheds, the UK’s biggest nightclub, and looks towards a return of his residency at Ibiza nightclub Unvrs, he will join us to answer your questions.

Known for playing a banging yet nuanced blend of house and techno, Cox’s career stretches back to the age of 10, learning his craft growing up in London and later Brighton, funding nights out by trimming his neighbours’ hedges. As Chicago house, Detroit techno and other new styles hit the UK, Cox was primed to receive them: fluidly mixing across three decks at once, he immersed himself in both the illegal rave scene and the new wave of nightclubs cropping up to showcase this music.

items.title: ‘My name was poison’: Donny Osmond on fame, failure – and his friend Michael Jackson
items.summary:
He was the child star of the Osmonds who become a global celebrity by 14. Then, at 21, his career came crashing down. Here, he reveals how he survived his years in exile – and what happened when Jackson was accused of child abuse

For a brief period in the early 1970s, Donny Osmond ruled the world. He was the global teenage heart-throb. Even Michael Jackson trailed behind him. He was 14 when his most famous song, Puppy Love, spent five weeks at No 1 in the UK. My sister had a huge poster of him on her bedroom wall. Then again, everybody’s sister had a poster of him on their bedroom wall. Between 1972 and 1973 he had six Top 5 hits in the UK, three of them No 1s (including The Twelfth of Never and Young Love). He was equally successful back home in the US.

Osmond was clean-cut, religious and respectful, with a mighty ability to punch out cover versions of saccharine standards. From his purple velvet cap to his doleful eyes and dazzling all-American smile, he was a marketing dream. We’d only just finished with Beatlemania. And now there was Donnymania.
